q: How do I count CO2 from burning coal washery rejects in a power plant?
title: Washery rejects as fuel: CO2
short: The same way as coal: tonnes burnt times carbon content times 44/12. Rejects carry much more ash and much less energy than run of mine coal, so the CO2 per tonne is lower but the CO2 per kWh is usually higher. Use a lab analysis of the rejects you burn, not a coal default.
audience: Fluidised bed power plants near Korba, Talcher and Dhanbad burning rejects, and the units buying their power

ul: Carbon content or gross calorific value from lab tests on each lot.
CO2 = tonnes x carbon fraction x 44/12, or energy x a coal factor matched to the rejects.

p: High ash lowers boiler efficiency and raises auxiliary power, so more fuel carbon is burnt for each kWh sent out. Calculate per kWh from your own heat rate.
The plant burning the rejects reports the CO2 as Scope 1. The washery that sells them does not count it again.
